Tutorials

One feature at a time: how to set it up, then every case you can run into, each with the real request and the real response. Every example was run against a self-hosted server: $AGENTRAAS_URL is http://localhost:13000 there, or https://agentraas.io on Cloud, and $AGENTRAAS_KEY is the agent's key from Connect agent.

The payment examples use mockpay, the built-in sandbox service, so nothing real is charged. It fails about one call in ten at random unless the payload says "fail": false, which is why the examples send it (the Failures tutorial sends "fail": true). Responses are shortened to the fields that matter (no timestamps or idempotency keys).

The whole loop in two minutes

  • Connect an agent and send an action
  • Safe retries (exactly once)
  • Validation rules

  • Spend caps and money caps
  • Action policies and allowed hours
  • Failures and the dead-letter queue
  • Undo an action
  • Record and replay
  • A support agent that refunds orders
  • Rules as code
  • Library mode and the chaos tester
  • LangChain and LangGraph tools
  • MCP: scan and wrap a server

Start here if you don't write code

AgentRaaS sits between your AI agent and the services it uses (Stripe, email, Slack and others). Before anything happens, it checks the action: it stops repeats, keeps to the limits you set, asks a person before big actions, and keeps a record you can read and undo.

What needs a developer, once: pointing the agent at AgentRaaS. If your agent runs in Make, Zapier or n8n, you can do it yourself: + Connect agent, pick Make, Zapier or another HTTP tool, and paste the settings it shows (see Connect and send).

Everything else is in the dashboard, no code:

  • Set limits an action must meet, like "amount at most 10000": Validation rules
  • Approve big actions before they run, also from your phone through a Slack, Teams, Telegram, Discord or email link: Human approval
  • Cap how much an agent can spend or do per day: Spend and money caps
  • Say what each agent may never do, or only do for your own email domains or office hours: Action policies
  • See every action and why it ran or stopped: Recent activity, click a row
  • Send a failed action again once the cause is fixed: Failed requests
  • Reverse an action, like refunding a charge: Undo
  • Let a support agent refund orders, but never more than half the order or a daily budget: A support agent that refunds orders

Each of those tutorials starts with In the dashboard, step by step: a recording and a picture for every click. You can skip the code boxes below it.

Words you will see

Agent
The AI program doing the work. Each one gets its own key.
Service and action
Where it acts and what it does there, like Stripe and charge.create (charge a card).
Payload
The details of one action, like the amount and the customer.
Success
It ran.
Deduplicated
A repeat of something that already ran, so it was not run again. The agent got the first answer back.
Blocked
One of your rules stopped it before it reached the service. Click the row to see which rule.
Pending approval
Waiting for a person to approve or deny it.
Error
The service itself refused it, for example a wrong key. It is listed in Failed requests.

Connect an agent and send an action

Every agent gets its own key. It sends each action to AgentRaaS, which checks it, runs it once and records it.

In the dashboard, step by step

No code needed. A recording of these exact clicks, then each step with a picture:

  1. Setup tab, Connect a service. Pick the service (here Stripe) and paste its API key. It is encrypted and never shown again.
  2. Give your agent (or your developer) the AgentRaaS URL and key shown here. The key is shown only once.
  3. One key per agent: + Connect agent, pick where it runs (here Make, Zapier or another no-code tool) and name it.
  4. Paste the setup text into your tool. When the agent makes its first call, it shows up here.
  5. Every call is listed under Recent activity. Click a row for its details.

With the API or in code

Or with the API (logged in as a member of the org):

POST /api/v1/agents/connect
{
  "org_id": "org_acme",
  "agent_id": "billing-agent",
  "label": "Billing agent"
}

It returns the agent's key and URLs:

{
  "api_key": "ar_live_...",
  "webhook_url": "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/billing-agent",
  "mcp_url": "$AGENTRAAS_URL/mcp"
}

Every case

Click a case to see the request and the real response.

A normal call runs200

The key matches the agent, so the call is checked, sent to the payment API once and recorded.

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/billing-agent" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTRAAS_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service": "mockpay", "action": "payment.create", "payload": {"customer": "cus_101", "amount": 1500, "fail": false}}'
{
  "forwarded": true,
  "upstream_id": "mockpay_5ccb9571edaaa7e5",
  "upstream_response": {
    "id": "mockpay_5ccb9571edaaa7e5",
    "amount": 1500,
    "status": "completed"
  },
  "reqId": "req_0057c6722f9baf6a"
}
A wrong key is refused401

Nothing is sent. Check the key in Connect agent, or regenerate it.

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/billing-agent" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ar_live_wrong" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service": "mockpay", "action": "payment.create", "payload": {"customer": "cus_101", "amount": 1500}}'
{
  "error": "Invalid or missing API key for this agent. Generate one from the dashboard's Connect Agent panel.",
  "reqId": "req_8d48b38526ebb8b3"
}
A key can't act as another agent401

Each key belongs to one agent. The support agent's key is refused on the billing agent's URL.

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/billing-agent" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SUPPORT_AGENT_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service": "mockpay", "action": "payment.create", "payload": {"customer": "cus_102", "amount": 900}}'
{
  "error": "Invalid or missing API key for this agent. Generate one from the dashboard's Connect Agent panel.",
  "reqId": "req_1bc28d81db487a81"
}
An unknown action is refused400

Only actions the service has, or custom actions you registered, can run.

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/billing-agent" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTRAAS_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service": "mockpay", "action": "payment.teleport", "payload": {"customer": "cus_103"}}'
{
  "error": "Unknown service.action: mockpay.payment.teleport",
  "reqId": "req_fac48a8552f52481"
}

Safe retries (exactly once)

An agent retries after a timeout, a crash or a loop. AgentRaaS recognises the same call and answers from its record, so the action runs once.

In the dashboard, step by step

No code needed. A recording of these exact clicks, then each step with a picture:

  1. Click Run live dedup test: 8 identical calls go to a sandbox and only 1 runs.
  2. Click a Deduplicated row to see why it was not sent again.

With the API or in code

  • Same agent, same service and action, same payload = the same call
  • Or send x-agentraas-idempotency-key: one key per action, never reused for a different payload

Every case

Click a case to see the request and the real response.

First call runs200

The call is new, so it runs and the result is stored.

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/billing-agent" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTRAAS_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service": "mockpay", "action": "payment.create", "payload": {"customer": "cus_201", "amount": 2500, "fail": false}}'
{
  "forwarded": true,
  "upstream_id": "mockpay_ca2bcc5e68218dc6",
  "upstream_response": {
    "id": "mockpay_ca2bcc5e68218dc6",
    "amount": 2500,
    "status": "completed"
  },
  "reqId": "req_bcb0cf24471610e6"
}
The retry is answered from the record200

"cached": true and the same payment id: the payment API was not called again.

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/billing-agent" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTRAAS_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service": "mockpay", "action": "payment.create", "payload": {"customer": "cus_201", "amount": 2500, "fail": false}}'
{
  "forwarded": true,
  "upstream_id": "mockpay_ca2bcc5e68218dc6",
  "upstream_response": {
    "id": "mockpay_ca2bcc5e68218dc6",
    "amount": 2500,
    "status": "completed"
  },
  "cached": true,
  "reqId": "req_48dab712c37896f2"
}
A different payload is a new call200

Another amount is another action, so it runs.

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/billing-agent" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTRAAS_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service": "mockpay", "action": "payment.create", "payload": {"customer": "cus_201", "amount": 3000, "fail": false}}'
{
  "forwarded": true,
  "upstream_id": "mockpay_18687154eba8aa7d",
  "upstream_response": {
    "id": "mockpay_18687154eba8aa7d",
    "amount": 3000,
    "status": "completed"
  },
  "reqId": "req_2f8286d9bd0ed0ec"
}
Your own idempotency key200

With x-agentraas-idempotency-key you name the action yourself, for example by your order id.

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/billing-agent" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTRAAS_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-agentraas-idempotency-key: order-5531" \
  -d '{"service": "mockpay", "action": "payment.create", "payload": {"customer": "cus_202", "amount": 700, "fail": false}}'
{
  "forwarded": true,
  "upstream_id": "mockpay_fbae3ca493558359",
  "upstream_response": {
    "id": "mockpay_fbae3ca493558359",
    "amount": 700,
    "status": "completed"
  },
  "reqId": "req_c4888769c1b4f441"
}
Same key, same body: answered from the record200

The retry carries the same key, so it is the same action.

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/billing-agent" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTRAAS_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-agentraas-idempotency-key: order-5531" \
  -d '{"service": "mockpay", "action": "payment.create", "payload": {"customer": "cus_202", "amount": 700, "fail": false}}'
{
  "forwarded": true,
  "upstream_id": "mockpay_fbae3ca493558359",
  "upstream_response": {
    "id": "mockpay_fbae3ca493558359",
    "amount": 700,
    "status": "completed"
  },
  "cached": true,
  "reqId": "req_8d7b9a38c31b9db6"
}
Same key, different body: refused422

A key stands for one exact action. Reusing it for something else is a bug in the caller, so it gets 422 and nothing runs.

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/billing-agent" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTRAAS_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-agentraas-idempotency-key: order-5531" \
  -d '{"service": "mockpay", "action": "payment.create", "payload": {"customer": "cus_202", "amount": 9900, "fail": false}}'
{
  "error": "This Idempotency-Key was already used with a different payload. Use a new key for a different request.",
  "reqId": "req_2afbde93e7f10218"
}

Validation rules

Check every payload before it is sent. A call that breaks a rule is refused with 422, nothing reaches the provider, and the answer tells the agent how to fix it.

In the dashboard, step by step

No code needed. A recording of these exact clicks, then each step with a picture:

  1. Rules tab, Validation rules. Name the service and action (Stripe, charge.create), then add a field: amount must be a number from 1 to 10000.
  2. Try it before saving: paste a sample and click Test. 50000 is too big, so it would be refused.
  3. Click Save rule. It is listed under Saved rules and applies right away.
  4. When an agent tries to charge 50000, the call is blocked and never reaches Stripe. The row says why.

With the API or in code

Rule used below: amount: a number from 100 to 10000, never above balance.

POST /api/v1/validation-rules
{
  "org_id": "org_acme",
  "service": "mockpay",
  "action": "payment.create",
  "fields": {
    "amount": {
      "type": "number",
      "min": 100,
      "max": 10000,
      "maxField": "balance"
    }
  }
}

Every case

Click a case to see the request and the real response.

A good payload runs200

Every field passes.

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/billing-agent" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTRAAS_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service": "mockpay", "action": "payment.create", "payload": {"customer": "cus_301", "amount": 4000, "balance": 9000, "fail": false}}'
{
  "forwarded": true,
  "upstream_id": "mockpay_de7d3b2cafeeb257",
  "upstream_response": {
    "id": "mockpay_de7d3b2cafeeb257",
    "amount": 4000,
    "status": "completed"
  },
  "reqId": "req_490edabf61d390e6"
}
Too big422

Above max: refused, nothing sent.

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/billing-agent" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTRAAS_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service": "mockpay", "action": "payment.create", "payload": {"customer": "cus_302", "amount": 50000, "balance": 90000}}'
{
  "error": "amount must be at most 10000",
  "reqId": "req_b77b85156f18c45c",
  "validation_errors": [
    {
      "field": "amount",
      "rule": "max",
      "message": "amount must be at most 10000",
      "hint": "Use a value of 10000 or less for \"amount\"."
    }
  ],
  "next_step": "Nothing was sent. Fix every field listed in validation_errors, following each hint, and send the call again."
}
Too small422

Below min.

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/billing-agent" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTRAAS_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service": "mockpay", "action": "payment.create", "payload": {"customer": "cus_303", "amount": 5, "balance": 9000}}'
{
  "error": "amount must be at least 100",
  "reqId": "req_0eb6f0cad08c05b2",
  "validation_errors": [
    {
      "field": "amount",
      "rule": "min",
      "message": "amount must be at least 100",
      "hint": "Use a value of 100 or more for \"amount\"."
    }
  ],
  "next_step": "Nothing was sent. Fix every field listed in validation_errors, following each hint, and send the call again."
}
Wrong type422

A string where a number belongs. The hint says what to send instead.

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/billing-agent" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTRAAS_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service": "mockpay", "action": "payment.create", "payload": {"customer": "cus_304", "amount": "forty", "balance": 9000}}'
{
  "error": "amount must be number, got string",
  "reqId": "req_b6a0703342901678",
  "validation_errors": [
    {
      "field": "amount",
      "rule": "type",
      "message": "amount must be number, got string",
      "hint": "Send \"amount\" as a number."
    }
  ],
  "next_step": "Nothing was sent. Fix every field listed in validation_errors, following each hint, and send the call again."
}
More than the balance422

amount may not be above the payload's own balance field.

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/billing-agent" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTRAAS_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service": "mockpay", "action": "payment.create", "payload": {"customer": "cus_305", "amount": 6000, "balance": 2000}}'
{
  "error": "amount (6000) must not exceed balance (2000)",
  "reqId": "req_73533228ce2ec5c9",
  "validation_errors": [
    {
      "field": "amount",
      "rule": "maxField",
      "message": "amount (6000) must not exceed balance (2000)",
      "hint": "Lower \"amount\" to 2000 or less, the current \"balance\"."
    }
  ],
  "next_step": "Nothing was sent. Fix every field listed in validation_errors, following each hint, and send the call again."
}

Human approval

Hold risky calls until a person says yes. The agent gets 202 and a status URL; the call runs once when approved, or never when denied.

In the dashboard, step by step

No code needed. A recording of these exact clicks, then each step with a picture:

  1. Rules tab, Approval rules. Hold Stripe charges when the amount is greater than 5000.
  2. Click Save rule.
  3. Monitor tab, Waiting for approval: the held call, with exactly what it wants to do.
  4. Approve runs the call once. The first decision wins, here or from Slack, Teams, Telegram, Discord or an email link.
  5. Deny drops it: the charge never happens and the agent is told it was denied.

With the API or in code

Rule used below: hold payment.create when amount > 5000.

POST /api/v1/hitl-rules
{
  "org_id": "org_acme",
  "service": "mockpay",
  "action": "payment.create",
  "field": "amount",
  "operator": "gt",
  "threshold": 5000
}

Every case

Click a case to see the request and the real response.

Under the threshold runs at once200

amount 3000 is not above 5000, so no approval is needed.

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/billing-agent" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTRAAS_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service": "mockpay", "action": "payment.create", "payload": {"customer": "cus_401", "amount": 3000, "fail": false}}'
{
  "forwarded": true,
  "upstream_id": "mockpay_c67428127ced4ca8",
  "upstream_response": {
    "id": "mockpay_c67428127ced4ca8",
    "amount": 3000,
    "status": "completed"
  },
  "reqId": "req_ecdc84ae3d625258"
}
Over the threshold is held202

The agent gets 202 and a status URL. Nothing has run yet.

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/billing-agent" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTRAAS_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service": "mockpay", "action": "payment.create", "payload": {"customer": "cus_402", "amount": 8000, "fail": false}}'
{
  "pending_approval": true,
  "reqId": "req_40ec2fe909bc7bb7"
}
A retry while it waits is not a second request409

The same call again gets 409 until someone decides.

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/billing-agent" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTRAAS_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service": "mockpay", "action": "payment.create", "payload": {"customer": "cus_402", "amount": 8000, "fail": false}}'
{
  "error": "An identical request is already being processed. Retry shortly.",
  "reqId": "req_655f70425b67fcd2"
}
Approve: the call runs once200

In the dashboard, Slack, an approval link, or agtrs approve. The held call runs now.

POST /api/v1/hitl/req_40ec2fe909bc7bb7/decide
{"decision": "approve"}

# or: agtrs approve req_40ec2fe909bc7bb7
{
  "reqId": "req_40ec2fe909bc7bb7",
  "status": "approved"
}
The agent checks its status URL200

The status URL now carries the result.

GET /v1/hitl/req_40ec2fe909bc7bb7
{
  "reqId": "req_40ec2fe909bc7bb7",
  "status": "approved",
  "result": {
    "forwarded": true,
    "upstream_id": "mockpay_d15a4f6b6f6360fe",
    "upstream_response": {
      "id": "mockpay_d15a4f6b6f6360fe",
      "amount": 8000,
      "status": "completed"
    }
  },
  "error": null
}
Another big charge is held202

A second request over the threshold.

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/billing-agent" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTRAAS_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service": "mockpay", "action": "payment.create", "payload": {"customer": "cus_403", "amount": 9500, "fail": false}}'
{
  "pending_approval": true,
  "reqId": "req_dece4fb358d5c279"
}
Deny: it never runs200

The call is dropped. Nothing reaches the payment API.

POST /api/v1/hitl/req_dece4fb358d5c279/decide
{"decision": "deny"}

# or: agtrs deny req_dece4fb358d5c279
{
  "reqId": "req_dece4fb358d5c279",
  "status": "denied"
}
The status URL says denied200

The agent can stop or ask for a smaller amount.

GET /v1/hitl/req_dece4fb358d5c279
{
  "reqId": "req_dece4fb358d5c279",
  "status": "denied",
  "result": null,
  "error": null
}

Spend caps and money caps

Limit how often an agent may act, or how much money it may move per day. Over the limit, the call is refused (429) or held for approval.

In the dashboard, step by step

No code needed. A recording of these exact clicks, then each step with a picture:

  1. Rules tab, Spend caps. billing-agent may charge at most 10000 in total per day on Stripe. Max calls caps the number of calls instead.
  2. Click Save rule. Leave Agent ID empty to cap every agent. "Route to approval" holds the call for a person instead of blocking it.
  3. The agent tries to charge 12000 today: over the daily total, so it is blocked before Stripe. The row says which cap stopped it.

With the API or in code

Rule used below: billing-agent: at most 2 payments an hour.

POST /api/v1/spend-cap-rules
{
  "org_id": "org_acme",
  "agent_id": "billing-agent",
  "service": "mockpay",
  "action": "payment.create",
  "window": "hour",
  "max_calls": 2,
  "on_exceed": "block"
}

Rule used below: all agents: at most 10000 in amount per day (Asia/Kolkata).

POST /api/v1/spend-cap-rules
{
  "org_id": "org_acme",
  "service": "mockpay",
  "action": "payment.create",
  "window": "day",
  "amount_field": "amount",
  "max_amount": 10000,
  "timezone": "Asia/Kolkata",
  "on_exceed": "block"
}

Rule used below: support-agent: 1 payment an hour, then ask a person.

POST /api/v1/spend-cap-rules
{
  "org_id": "org_acme",
  "agent_id": "support-agent",
  "service": "mockpay",
  "action": "payment.create",
  "window": "hour",
  "max_calls": 1,
  "on_exceed": "hitl"
}

Action policies and allowed hours

Decide what each agent may do at all: deny an action, require a field to match (an email domain), or allow it only during working hours. A refused call gets 403 naming the policy.

In the dashboard, step by step

No code needed. A recording of these exact clicks, then each step with a picture:

  1. Rules tab, Action policies. support-agent may send email (Resend) only to addresses at acme.com.
  2. Click Save policy. "Never allow" blocks an action outright; allowed hours limit when it may run.
  3. The agent tries to email someone@gmail.com: blocked, the email is never sent. The row names the policy.

With the API or in code

Rule used below: support-agent may not use mockpay at all.

POST /api/v1/action-policies
{
  "org_id": "org_acme",
  "agent_id": "support-agent",
  "service": "mockpay",
  "action": "*",
  "effect": "deny"
}

Rule used below: receipts only go to acme.com addresses.

POST /api/v1/action-policies
{
  "org_id": "org_acme",
  "service": "mockpay",
  "action": "payment.create",
  "effect": "require",
  "fields": {
    "receipt_email": {
      "domains": [
        "acme.com"
      ]
    }
  }
}

Rule used below: refunds only on tue, wed, thu, fri, sat, sun, 09:00 to 17:00 UTC.

POST /api/v1/action-policies
{
  "org_id": "org_acme",
  "service": "mockpay",
  "action": "payment.refund",
  "effect": "require",
  "hours": {
    "tz": "UTC",
    "days": [
      "tue",
      "wed",
      "thu",
      "fri",
      "sat",
      "sun"
    ],
    "from": "09:00",
    "to": "17:00"
  }
}

Every case

Click a case to see the request and the real response.

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/support-agent" \

  -d '{"service": "mockpay", "action": "payment.create", "payload": {"customer": "cus_601", "amount": 100, "receipt_email": "pat@acme.com", "fail": false}}'
{
  "error": "This agent may not call mockpay.payment.create (action policy #171)",

}

{

Failures and the dead-letter queue

When the provider fails, the agent gets the error and the call is kept in the dead-letter queue, with its payload, to replay later. Nothing is silently lost.

In the dashboard, step by step

No code needed. A recording of these exact clicks, then each step with a picture:

  1. Monitor tab, Failed requests: every call the service itself refused, with its error (here Stripe: invalid API key).
  2. Fix the cause first (here: paste the right key in Setup, Credentials). Then click Replay, or Edit & Replay to change the payload first.
  3. A replayed call that succeeds leaves the list. Dismiss removes one you do not want to send.

With the API or in code

Every case

Click a case to see the request and the real response.

The provider fails500

mockpay with fail: true always errors (it stands in for a provider outage). The agent gets the error.

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/billing-agent" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTRAAS_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service": "mockpay", "action": "payment.create", "payload": {"customer": "cus_701", "amount": 1200, "fail": true}}'
{
  "error": "MockPay temporarily unavailable",
  "reqId": "req_b285aba574f7e48b",
  "agentraas_note": "Request blocked by AgentRaaS."
}
It is in the dead-letter queue200

Monitor › Failed requests, or the API, lists it with the error.

GET /api/v1/dead-letter-queue?org_id=org_acme
{
  "entries": [
    {
      "id": 417,
      "req_id": "req_b285aba574f7e48b",
      "org_id": "org_acme",
      "agent_id": "billing-agent",
      "service": "mockpay",
      "action": "payment.create",
      "error_message": "MockPay temporarily unavailable",
      "created_at": "2026-10-26T09:14:11.784907Z",
      "payload": {
        "customer": "cus_701",
        "amount": 1200,
        "fail": true
      }
    }
  ]
}
Replay it500

Sent again with the same Idempotency-Key, so it still runs at most once. This payload still says fail: true, so it fails again ("replayed": false); once a real provider is back, the replay runs it.

POST /api/v1/dead-letter-queue/417/replay
{
  "error": "MockPay temporarily unavailable",
  "replayed": false,
  "reqId": "req_0b1139f08b54f626"
}
Repeated failures open the circuit breaker503

Calls to mockpay now get 503 at once, without being sent, so a broken provider is not hammered and the agent can back off.

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/billing-agent" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTRAAS_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service": "mockpay", "action": "payment.create", "payload": {"customer": "cus_710", "amount": 1200, "fail": false}}'
{
  "error": "Circuit breaker open for mockpay. Try again later.",
  "reqId": "req_a8daa75cdfbe5233"
}
After 30 seconds, one call is let through200

It works, so the breaker closes and calls flow again.

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/billing-agent" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTRAAS_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service": "mockpay", "action": "payment.create", "payload": {"customer": "cus_711", "amount": 1200, "fail": false}}'
{
  "forwarded": true,
  "upstream_id": "mockpay_e711d951ab5b8ea9",
  "upstream_response": {
    "id": "mockpay_e711d951ab5b8ea9",
    "amount": 1200,
    "status": "completed"
  },
  "reqId": "req_dce3332d7b95c756"
}
Back to normal200

The next call runs as usual.

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/billing-agent" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTRAAS_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service": "mockpay", "action": "payment.create", "payload": {"customer": "cus_712", "amount": 1200, "fail": false}}'
{
  "forwarded": true,
  "upstream_id": "mockpay_b84fafbdfff98f83",
  "upstream_response": {
    "id": "mockpay_b84fafbdfff98f83",
    "amount": 1200,
    "status": "completed"
  },
  "reqId": "req_e1592a116f983748"
}

Undo an action

Reverse something an agent did: a charge is refunded, a Slack message deleted, your own action reversed by the action you named. Each one can be undone once, for 30 days.

In the dashboard, step by step

No code needed. A recording of these exact clicks, then each step with a picture:

  1. Monitor tab, Undo actions: what each one will run to reverse it (here a refund).
  2. Click Undo, then Confirm undo.
  3. The refund runs once. The entry is marked undone and cannot be undone twice.

With the API or in code

Every case

Click a case to see the request and the real response.

A charge runs200

It has a known reverse (payment.refund), so it is recorded as undoable.

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/billing-agent" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTRAAS_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \

{

    "status": "completed"

  "reqId": "req_a8f37613d5851054"
}
It appears in Undo actions200

With what undoing it will run.

GET /api/v1/undo-log?org_id=org_acme
{
  "entries": [
    {
      "id": 2264,
      "req_id": "req_a8f37613d5851054",

        "payment": "mockpay_591cb571360f9704"

  "undone": true,

A second undo is refused409

Record and replay

Record a run against the real providers once, then replay it in tests: every call is answered from the recording and nothing reaches the provider.

In the dashboard, step by step

No code needed. A recording of these exact clicks, then each step with a picture:

  1. Monitor tab, Recordings: each recorded run, how many calls it made and when.
  2. Click View to see every call and its answer. A replay is answered from here, so nothing reaches the real service.

With the API or in code

  • Python: Client(..., record="refund-flow") or replay="refund-flow", run_id=...
  • JS: record / replay / runId in the Client options

A support agent that refunds orders

A customer says an item was missing. The support agent refunds it, but never more than half of what the order really cost, and never more than a day's budget. AgentRaaS reads the order itself, so the agent can't talk its way past the limit.

In the dashboard, step by step

No code needed. A recording of these exact clicks, then each step with a picture:

  1. Rules tab, Action policies. A refund by support-agent may be at most half the order. AgentRaaS reads the order itself (order.get), so the agent cannot send a bigger order amount. Over the limit: Route to approval.
  2. Spend caps: at most 1500 in refunds a day for support-agent, counted in India time.
  3. The 150 refund ran. The 700 one is over half the order, so it waits here for a person: Monitor tab, Waiting for approval.
  4. Later that day: 600 more ran, then 900 would pass the 1500 a day, so it was blocked. The row says which cap stopped it.

With the API or in code

Rule used below: support-agent: up to half the order runs; more goes to a person.

POST /api/v1/action-policies
{
  "org_id": "org_acme",
  "agent_id": "support-agent",
  "service": "mockpay",
  "action": "payment.refund",
  "effect": "require",
  "fields": {
    "amount": {
      "max_from": {
        "action": "order.get",
        "with": {
          "order_id": "order_id"
        },
        "field": "order_amount",
        "factor": 0.5
      }
    }
  },
  "on_violation": "hitl"
}

Rule used below: support-agent: at most 1500 in refunds a day (India time).

POST /api/v1/spend-cap-rules
{
  "org_id": "org_acme",
  "agent_id": "support-agent",
  "service": "mockpay",
  "action": "payment.refund",
  "window": "day",
  "amount_field": "amount",
  "max_amount": 1500,
  "timezone": "Asia/Kolkata",
  "on_exceed": "block"
}
  • The examples use the sandbox: an order id ends in its amount (order_1200 is an order of 1200). With Cashfree the read is cashfree order.get and the field is order_amount; with Razorpay it is payment.get, field amount, minus amount_refunded
  • A refund with no amount, a missing order id or an order the provider can't find is never sent unchecked: it goes to approval too

Every case

Click a case to see the request and the real response.

A missing item: refund 150 of a 1200 order200

AgentRaaS reads the order itself (1200). 150 is under half, so the refund runs.

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/support-agent" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTRAAS_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service": "mockpay", "action": "payment.refund", "payload": {"payment": "mockpay_ord1200", "order_id": "order_1200", "amount": 150}}'
{
  "forwarded": true,
  "upstream_id": "mockrefund_b1025b2d7afd3ca9",
  "upstream_response": {
    "id": "mockrefund_b1025b2d7afd3ca9",
    "payment": "mockpay_ord1200",
    "status": "refunded"
  },
  "reqId": "req_0684a4a6cbf550ff"
}
The same refund, retried200

The agent timed out and asked again: answered from the record, the customer is refunded once.

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/support-agent" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTRAAS_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service": "mockpay", "action": "payment.refund", "payload": {"payment": "mockpay_ord1200", "order_id": "order_1200", "amount": 150}}'
{
  "forwarded": true,
  "upstream_id": "mockrefund_b1025b2d7afd3ca9",
  "upstream_response": {
    "id": "mockrefund_b1025b2d7afd3ca9",
    "payment": "mockpay_ord1200",
    "status": "refunded"
  },
  "cached": true,
  "reqId": "req_51dd572bf3efdc01"
}
More than half the order waits for a person202

700 of a 1200 order is over the limit: held, 202 and a status URL. Nothing is refunded until someone approves.

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/support-agent" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTRAAS_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \

{
  "pending_approval": true,
  "reqId": "req_293bf54eb4a8916e"
}
No amount is not a full refund202

Leaving the amount out means "refund everything" to many providers. It can't be checked, so it is held too.

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/support-agent" \

{

A second refund today200

600 of a 1300 order is under half; 750 refunded today so far.

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/support-agent" \

Rules as code

Keep rules in a YAML file in your repo, review changes like code, and apply them from CI. agentraas apply makes the server match the file; running it twice changes nothing.

Set it up

pip install "agentraas[apply]"

agentraas.yaml:

apiVersion: agentraas.io/v1alpha1
kind: ValidationRule
metadata: {name: sane-amounts, org: org_acme}
spec: {service: mockpay, action: payment.create, fields: {amount: {type: number, max: 10000}}}
---
apiVersion: agentraas.io/v1alpha1
kind: SpendCap
metadata: {name: refund-budget, org: org_acme}
spec: {service: mockpay, action: payment.refund, window: day, maxCalls: 20, onExceed: block}
  • AGENTRAAS_URL=http://localhost:13000
  • AGENTRAAS_EMAIL / AGENTRAAS_PASSWORD: a user who can change the org

Every case

Click a case to see the request and the real response.

Preview the planexit 0

--dry-run prints what would change and changes nothing.

$ agtrs apply -f agentraas.yaml --dry-run
+ ValidationRule org_acme mockpay.payment.create (sane-amounts)
+ SpendCap org_acme mockpay.payment.refund (refund-budget)
Apply itexit 0

Creates what is missing.

$ agtrs apply -f agentraas.yaml
+ ValidationRule org_acme mockpay.payment.create (sane-amounts)
+ SpendCap org_acme mockpay.payment.refund (refund-budget)
Apply again: nothing to doexit 0

The server already matches the file.

$ agtrs apply -f agentraas.yaml
no changes
Change a limit in the fileexit 0

max 10000 becomes 5000; apply replaces the rule that changed.

$ agtrs apply -f agentraas.yaml   # after changing max: 10000 to max: 5000
+ ValidationRule org_acme mockpay.payment.create (sane-amounts)
Remove a rule with --pruneexit 0

Without --prune, rules missing from the file are left alone. With it, they are deleted.

$ agtrs apply -f agentraas.yaml --prune   # after deleting the SpendCap from the file
- SpendCap org_acme mockpay.payment.refund (id 288)
A mistake fails the CI jobexit 1

An unknown kind is reported and the command exits non-zero, so the pipeline stops.

$ agtrs apply -f agentraas.yaml   # with a typo: kind: SpendLimit
agentraas.yaml document 2: kind must be one of DedupRule, ValidationRule, ActionPolicy, SpendCap

Library mode and the chaos tester

No server at all: a decorator makes a function with side effects run once, even when it is retried, and the chaos tester finds the calls that would run twice.

Set it up

pip install agentraas

Every case

Click a case to see the request and the real response.

Wrap a function: a retry runs it onceexit 0

The second call with the same arguments returns the stored result; the function body does not run.

lib_demo.py

from agentraas.local import exactly_once

calls = 0

@exactly_once()                 # state in a local SQLite file
def charge(customer, amount):
    global calls
    calls += 1
    print(f"  charging {customer} {amount}")
    return f"ch_{customer}_{amount}"

print(charge("cus_42", 4200))   # runs
print(charge("cus_42", 4200))   # retry: cached, no second charge
print(charge("cus_42", 900))    # different arguments: runs
print("times charged:", calls)
$ python lib_demo.py
  charging cus_42 4200
ch_cus_42_4200
ch_cus_42_4200
  charging cus_42 900
ch_cus_42_900
times charged: 2
A failure is not cachedexit 0

If the function raises, nothing is stored, so the retry runs for real.

err_demo.py

from agentraas.local import exactly_once

attempts = 0

@exactly_once()
def send_invoice(customer):
    global attempts
    attempts += 1
    if attempts == 1:
        raise TimeoutError("provider timed out")
    return f"inv_{customer}"

for _ in range(2):
    try:
        print(send_invoice("cus_77"))
    except TimeoutError as e:
        print("  failed:", e, "(not cached, a retry runs again)")
print("attempts:", attempts)
$ python err_demo.py
  failed: provider timed out (not cached, a retry runs again)
inv_cus_77
attempts: 2
The chaos tester finds a double chargeexit 1

It lets each write run, then drops the response. The agent retries without an idempotency key, and the charge runs twice.

agent.py

import os, requests
API = os.environ["AGENTRAAS_CHAOS_URL"]

def charge(customer, amount):
    for attempt in range(3):          # retry on network errors
        try:
            return requests.post(f"{API}/v1/charges",
                                 data={"customer": customer, "amount": amount}, timeout=5).json()
        except requests.RequestException:
            continue

charge("cus_42", 4200)
$ agentraas chaos --mock -- python agent.py
agentraas-chaos listening on http://127.0.0.1:8787 -> mock (fault: lost-response)
agentraas-chaos: 2 write requests, 1 responses dropped after execution

  DUPLICATES: 1 action(s) executed more than once

    2x  POST /v1/charges  (body sha256 a32934913660)

  Fix: send an Idempotency-Key header that stays the same across retries, for
  providers that honor one. With agentraas.local.exactly_once, give the function an
  `idempotency_key` parameter and send it as that header; for providers without
  idempotency support, route the call through an AgentRaaS server.
With exactly_once and an idempotency key it passesexit 0

The retry carries the same key, so nothing doubles. Exit code 0, so CI passes.

agent_fixed.py

import os, requests
from agentraas.local import exactly_once
API = os.environ["AGENTRAAS_CHAOS_URL"]

@exactly_once()
def charge(customer, amount, idempotency_key=None):
    for attempt in range(3):
        try:
            return requests.post(f"{API}/v1/charges",
                                 data={"customer": customer, "amount": amount},
                                 headers={"Idempotency-Key": idempotency_key}, timeout=5).json()
        except requests.RequestException:
            continue

charge("cus_42", 4200)
$ agentraas chaos --mock -- python agent_fixed.py
agentraas-chaos listening on http://127.0.0.1:8787 -> mock (fault: lost-response)
agentraas-chaos: 2 write requests, 1 responses dropped after execution

  No duplicates: every retried write was deduplicated or never retried.

  Protected by an idempotency key: 1 retry

LangChain and LangGraph tools

Wrap the tools that have side effects. When the model calls one again with the same arguments, or the graph re-runs after a crash, the stored result comes back instead of a second action.

Set it up

pip install "agentraas[langchain]"
  • CrewAI: from agentraas.crewai import protect_tool, same idea
  • Vercel AI SDK: protectTools in the npm package

Every case

Click a case to see the request and the real response.

Protect a toolexit 0

Use the protected tool wherever the agent takes its tools: create_react_agent, ToolNode, an AgentExecutor.

lc_demo.py

from langchain_core.tools import tool
from agentraas.langchain import protect_tool

sent = []

@tool
def send_refund(customer: str, amount: int) -> str:
    """Refund a customer."""
    sent.append((customer, amount))
    return f"refund {len(sent)} sent to {customer}"

safe = protect_tool(send_refund)

print(safe.invoke({"customer": "cus_9", "amount": 500}))   # runs
print(safe.invoke({"customer": "cus_9", "amount": 500}))   # model repeats itself: stored result
print(safe.invoke({"customer": "cus_9", "amount": 700}))   # different arguments: runs
print("refunds actually sent:", len(sent))
$ python lc_demo.py
refund 1 sent to cus_9
refund 1 sent to cus_9
refund 2 sent to cus_9
refunds actually sent: 2

MCP: scan and wrap a server

agentraas scan lists which tools of an MCP server can move money, delete data or send messages. agentraas wrap puts exactly-once in front of the server, so a retrying or looping model cannot run the same write twice.

Set it up

pip install agentraas

claude_desktop_config.json:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "billing": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": [
        "agentraas",
        "wrap",
        "--",
        "python",
        "billing_server.py"
      ]
    }
  }
}

Every case

Click a case to see the request and the real response.

Scan the serverexit 0

Starts it, asks only for its tool list, and sorts the tools by risk. Nothing is called.

billing_server.py

import json, sys, collections
# A small demo billing MCP server (stdio), written for this tutorial.
count = collections.Counter()
TOOLS = [
    {"name": "get_invoice", "description": "Look up an invoice", "inputSchema": {"type": "object"}},
    {"name": "update_note", "description": "Edit a customer note", "inputSchema": {"type": "object"}},
    {"name": "send_receipt", "description": "Email a receipt", "inputSchema": {"type": "object"}},
    {"name": "create_refund", "description": "Refund a payment", "inputSchema": {"type": "object"}},
    {"name": "delete_customer", "description": "Delete a customer", "inputSchema": {"type": "object"}},
]
for line in sys.stdin:
    msg = json.loads(line)
    if "id" not in msg:
        continue
    m, rid = msg["method"], msg["id"]
    if m == "initialize":
        res = {"protocolVersion": "2025-06-18", "capabilities": {"tools": {}}, "serverInfo": {"name": "billing-demo", "version": "1"}}
    elif m == "tools/list":
        res = {"tools": TOOLS}
    elif m == "tools/call":
        name = msg["params"]["name"]; count[name] += 1
        res = {"content": [{"type": "text", "text": f"{name} ran (time #{count[name]})"}], "isError": False}
    else:
        res = {}
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": rid, "result": res}) + "\n"); sys.stdout.flush()
$ agentraas scan -- python billing_server.py

billing_server.py  (python billing_server.py)
  5 tools: 3 high risk, 1 write, 1 read-only
    HIGH    deletes    delete_customer  (name: delete)
    HIGH    money      create_refund  (name: refund)
    HIGH    sends      send_receipt  (name: send)
    MEDIUM  writes     update_note  (name: update)
  Fix duplicates and get an audit log: agentraas wrap -- python billing_server.py

High-risk tools can spend money, delete data or reach people. To block, cap or hold them for
human approval before they run, route them through an AgentRaaS server: https://agentraas.io/mcp-scan
Scan in CIexit 0

--fail-on high exits non-zero when a high-risk tool is present, so a new dangerous tool needs a review.

$ agentraas scan --fail-on high -- python billing_server.py; echo "exit code: $?"

billing_server.py  (python billing_server.py)
  5 tools: 3 high risk, 1 write, 1 read-only
    HIGH    deletes    delete_customer  (name: delete)
    HIGH    money      create_refund  (name: refund)
    HIGH    sends      send_receipt  (name: send)
    MEDIUM  writes     update_note  (name: update)
  Fix duplicates and get an audit log: agentraas wrap -- python billing_server.py

High-risk tools can spend money, delete data or reach people. To block, cap or hold them for
human approval before they run, route them through an AgentRaaS server: https://agentraas.io/mcp-scan
exit code: 1
A write tool runsexit 0

Through agentraas wrap, the first refund runs.

$ tools/call create_refund {"payment": "pay_1", "amount": 500}
create_refund ran (time #1)
The model repeats it: answered from the recordexit 0

Same tool, same arguments inside the window (10 minutes by default): the stored result, marked deduplicated.

$ tools/call create_refund {"payment": "pay_1", "amount": 500}
create_refund ran (time #1)   _meta: {"agentraas/deduplicated": true}
Different arguments runexit 0

Another refund is another action.

$ tools/call create_refund {"payment": "pay_2", "amount": 500}
create_refund ran (time #2)
Read tools always runexit 0

get_* and other read-only tools are never deduplicated, so lookups stay fresh.

$ tools/call get_invoice {"id": "inv_1"}
get_invoice ran (time #1)
...every timeexit 0

$ tools/call get_invoice {"id": "inv_1"}
get_invoice ran (time #2)
Every call is in the audit logexit 0

~/.agentraas/mcp-audit.jsonl by default (--log to change it).

$ tail -n 3 ~/.agentraas/mcp-audit.jsonl

Recipes for real services

How to connect a service people already use, what an agent can do with it, and one rule worth adding first. The rule bodies were saved against a real server; the calls need your own key, so they show no response.

  • Stripe
  • Slack
  • Resend
  • GitHub
  • Razorpay
  • Cashfree Payments
  • RazorpayX Payouts
  • Gupshup (WhatsApp)
  • MSG91 (SMS)
  • Delhivery
  • Paypal

Stripe

Charge cards, refund, manage customers and subscriptions.

Connect it

Setup tab, Connect a service, pick Stripe and paste the Secret key. Starts with sk_test_ or sk_live_. Try a test key first. Where to find it.

A charge can be undone (refunded) from Undo actions.

What your agent can call

  • charge.create: needs currency, customer (can be undone)
  • customer.create
  • charge.refund: needs charge
  • payment_intent.create: needs amount, currency
  • payment_intent.refund: needs payment_intent
  • subscription.create: needs customer, items (can be undone)
  • subscription.cancel: needs id
  • invoice.create: needs customer

A first rule

Hold charges above 50000 for a person. Stripe counts in cents, so that is 500.00 USD. In the dashboard: Rules tab. With the API:

POST /api/v1/hitl-rules
{
  "org_id": "org_acme",
  "service": "stripe",
  "action": "charge.create",
  "field": "amount",
  "operator": "gt",
  "threshold": 50000
}

A call

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/billing-agent" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTRAAS_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service": "stripe", "action": "charge.create", "payload": {"amount": 2500, "currency": "usd", "customer": "cus_123"}}'

Slack

Post and delete messages.

Connect it

Setup tab, Connect a service, pick Slack and paste the Bot token. Starts with xoxb-. Invite the bot to the channel. Where to find it.

Invite the bot to each channel first. A posted message can be undone (deleted).

What your agent can call

  • message.post: needs channel, text (can be undone)
  • message.postEphemeral: needs channel, user, text
  • message.delete: needs channel, ts

A first rule

Post only to #support and #alerts. Any other channel is blocked, and the error names the rule. In the dashboard: Rules tab. With the API:

POST /api/v1/action-policies
{
  "org_id": "org_acme",
  "service": "slack",
  "action": "message.post",
  "effect": "require",
  "fields": {
    "channel": {
      "enum": [
        "#support",
        "#alerts"
      ]
    }
  }
}

A call

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/billing-agent" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTRAAS_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service": "slack", "action": "message.post", "payload": {"channel": "#support", "text": "Ticket 4182 was refunded."}}'

Resend

Send email.

Connect it

Setup tab, Connect a service, pick Resend and paste the API key. Starts with re_. Send from a domain you verified in Resend. Where to find it.

Send from a domain you verified in Resend. An email cannot be undone, so this is a good place for a rule.

What your agent can call

  • email.send: needs from, to, subject

A first rule

Send only to addresses at acme.com, so an agent can never email outside the company. In the dashboard: Rules tab. With the API:

POST /api/v1/action-policies
{
  "org_id": "org_acme",
  "service": "resend",
  "action": "email.send",
  "effect": "require",
  "fields": {
    "to": {
      "domains": [
        "acme.com"
      ]
    }
  }
}

A call

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/billing-agent" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTRAAS_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service": "resend", "action": "email.send", "payload": {"from": "help@acme.com", "to": "jo@acme.com", "subject": "Your refund", "text": "It is on its way."}}'

GitHub

Open, comment on and update issues.

Connect it

Setup tab, Connect a service, pick GitHub and paste the Fine-grained personal access token. Give it Issues: read and write on the repositories your agent uses. Where to find it.

A fine-grained token with Issues: read and write on just the repositories the agent uses.

What your agent can call

  • issue.create: needs owner, repo, title
  • issue.comment: needs owner, repo, issue_number, body
  • issue.update: needs owner, repo, issue_number

A first rule

At most 20 new issues a day, so an agent stuck in a loop cannot flood the repository. In the dashboard: Rules tab. With the API:

POST /api/v1/spend-cap-rules
{
  "org_id": "org_acme",
  "service": "github",
  "action": "issue.create",
  "window": "day",
  "max_calls": 20,
  "on_exceed": "block"
}

A call

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/billing-agent" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTRAAS_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service": "github", "action": "issue.create", "payload": {"owner": "your-org", "repo": "your-repo", "title": "Checkout fails on Safari"}}'

Razorpay

Create payment orders (India).

Connect it

Setup tab, Connect a service, pick Razorpay and paste the Key ID and Key secret. Where to find it.

Razorpay takes two values: the Key ID and the Key secret. Use test mode keys while you try it. For refunds, payment.refund can be held to what is left of the payment: max_from with action payment.get, field amount, minus amount_refunded.

What your agent can call

  • payment.create: needs currency
  • payment.get: needs payment_id
  • payment.refund: needs payment_id

A first rule

Hold orders above 500000 for a person. Razorpay counts in paise, so that is 5,000 rupees. In the dashboard: Rules tab. With the API:

POST /api/v1/hitl-rules
{
  "org_id": "org_acme",
  "service": "razorpay",
  "action": "payment.create",
  "field": "amount",
  "operator": "gt",
  "threshold": 500000
}

A call

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/billing-agent" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTRAAS_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service": "razorpay", "action": "payment.create", "payload": {"amount": 49900, "currency": "INR"}}'

Cashfree Payments

Take payments and refund orders (India).

Connect it

Setup tab, Connect a service, pick Cashfree Payments and paste the App ID and Secret key. Where to find it.

Cashfree takes two values: the App ID and the Secret key. Pick Cashfree Payments (test) for sandbox keys. Every refund carries an idempotency key, so a retried refund runs once.

What your agent can call

  • order.create: needs order_amount, order_currency, customer_details
  • order.get: needs order_id
  • refund.create: needs order_id, refund_amount, refund_id

A first rule

A refund up to half of what the order really cost runs; more goes to a person. AgentRaaS reads the order from Cashfree itself, so the agent cannot send a bigger order amount (see Limits the server looks up in the docs). In the dashboard: Rules tab. With the API:

POST /api/v1/action-policies
{
  "org_id": "org_acme",
  "service": "cashfree",
  "action": "refund.create",
  "effect": "require",
  "fields": {
    "refund_amount": {
      "max_from": {
        "action": "order.get",
        "with": {
          "order_id": "order_id"
        },
        "field": "order_amount",
        "factor": 0.5
      }
    }
  },
  "on_violation": "hitl"
}

A call

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/billing-agent" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTRAAS_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service": "cashfree", "action": "refund.create", "payload": {"order_id": "order_1001", "refund_amount": 150, "refund_id": "rf_1001_missing_milk"}}'

RazorpayX Payouts

Pay riders, sellers and vendors from your RazorpayX account.

Connect it

Setup tab, Connect a service, pick RazorpayX Payouts and paste the Key ID and Key secret. Where to find it.

RazorpayX requires an idempotency key on every payout. AgentRaaS sends one (X-Payout-Idempotency) that stays the same when the agent retries, so a timed-out payout is not paid twice.

What your agent can call

  • payout.create: needs account_number, fund_account_id, amount, currency, mode, purpose
  • payout.get: needs payout_id

A first rule

At most 5000000 in payouts a day (paise, so 50,000 rupees), counted in India time; past that, a person approves each one. In the dashboard: Rules tab. With the API:

POST /api/v1/spend-cap-rules
{
  "org_id": "org_acme",
  "service": "razorpayx",
  "action": "payout.create",
  "window": "day",
  "amount_field": "amount",
  "max_amount": 5000000,
  "timezone": "Asia/Kolkata",
  "on_exceed": "hitl"
}

A call

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/billing-agent" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTRAAS_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service": "razorpayx", "action": "payout.create", "payload": {"account_number": "7878780080316316", "fund_account_id": "fa_00000000000001", "amount": 50000, "currency": "INR", "mode": "IMPS", "purpose": "payout", "reference_id": "rider-4182-oct-26"}}'

Gupshup (WhatsApp)

Send WhatsApp messages: order updates, delivery and support.

Connect it

Setup tab, Connect a service, pick Gupshup (WhatsApp) and paste the API key. From your Gupshup account. Send from the WhatsApp number and app registered there. Where to find it.

message is a JSON string, as Gupshup expects it. source is your WhatsApp Business number and src.name the app name registered with it.

What your agent can call

  • message.send: needs channel, source, destination, src.name, message

A first rule

Only between 09:00 and 21:00 India time, so an agent stuck in a loop never messages customers at night. The same message to the same number is sent once anyway. In the dashboard: Rules tab. With the API:

POST /api/v1/action-policies
{
  "org_id": "org_acme",
  "service": "gupshup",
  "action": "message.send",
  "effect": "require",
  "hours": {
    "tz": "Asia/Kolkata",
    "from": "09:00",
    "to": "21:00"
  }
}

A call

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/billing-agent" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTRAAS_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service": "gupshup", "action": "message.send", "payload": {"channel": "whatsapp", "source": "917834811114", "destination": "919876543210", "src.name": "YourApp", "message": "{\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":\"Your order is on its way.\"}"}}'

MSG91 (SMS)

Send SMS from a DLT-approved template: OTPs, order and delivery updates (India).

Connect it

Setup tab, Connect a service, pick MSG91 (SMS) and paste the Auth key. From the MSG91 panel, Authkey. Sends a DLT-approved template. MSG91 answers success before it checks the key, so a wrong key shows up only in MSG91's delivery reports. Where to find it.

Each recipient carries the variables of your template by name. MSG91 answers success before it checks the key, so check its delivery reports after the first send.

What your agent can call

  • flow.send: needs template_id, recipients

A first rule

At most 500 sends a day, counted in India time, so an agent stuck in a loop cannot run up an SMS bill. The same send to the same numbers runs once anyway. In the dashboard: Rules tab. With the API:

POST /api/v1/spend-cap-rules
{
  "org_id": "org_acme",
  "service": "msg91",
  "action": "flow.send",
  "window": "day",
  "max_calls": 500,
  "timezone": "Asia/Kolkata",
  "on_exceed": "block"
}

A call

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/billing-agent" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTRAAS_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service": "msg91", "action": "flow.send", "payload": {"template_id": "your_template_id", "short_url": "0", "recipients": [{"mobiles": "919876543210", "order": "1001"}]}}'

Delhivery

Create shipments, track waybills and check pincodes (India).

Connect it

Setup tab, Connect a service, pick Delhivery and paste the API token. From Delhivery One, Settings, API setup. shipment.create sends format "json" and data: the shipments JSON as a string. Where to find it.

shipment.create sends format "json" and data, the shipments JSON as a string, as Delhivery expects it. Pick Delhivery (test) for a staging token.

What your agent can call

  • shipment.track: needs waybill
  • pincode.check: needs filter_codes
  • shipment.create: needs format, data

A first rule

Up to 200 new shipments a day, counted in India time; past that, a person approves each one, so a loop cannot book pickups by the hundred. In the dashboard: Rules tab. With the API:

POST /api/v1/spend-cap-rules
{
  "org_id": "org_acme",
  "service": "delhivery",
  "action": "shipment.create",
  "window": "day",
  "max_calls": 200,
  "timezone": "Asia/Kolkata",
  "on_exceed": "hitl"
}

A call

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/billing-agent" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTRAAS_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service": "delhivery", "action": "shipment.track", "payload": {"waybill": "1234567890123"}}'

Paypal

Create checkout orders.

Connect it

Setup tab, Connect a service, pick Paypal and paste the access token.

PayPal is not in Connect a service yet: save an access token under Setup, Credentials (service paypal). PayPal access tokens expire, so it has to be replaced when it does.

What your agent can call

  • order.create: needs intent, purchase_units

A first rule

Hold every order for a person. The amount sits inside purchase_units, where amount rules cannot reach it, so this rule has no threshold. In the dashboard: Rules tab. With the API:

POST /api/v1/hitl-rules
{
  "org_id": "org_acme",
  "service": "paypal",
  "action": "order.create"
}

A call

curl -X POST "$AGENTRAAS_URL/v1/webhook/org_acme/billing-agent" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTRAAS_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service": "paypal", "action": "order.create", "payload": {"intent": "CAPTURE", "purchase_units": [{"amount": {"currency_code": "USD", "value": "25.00"}}]}}'
